newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open firm after Wall Street pick-up.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open firm after Wall Street pick-up.

text.p: Australian shares opened slightly firmer on Tuesday after Wall Street halted a two-session steep slide on Monday.
At 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 5.7 points firmer at 2,672.9.
The September share price index was up 12 points at 2,668 and at a 4.9 point discount to the underlying index.

Early trade was dominated by Australia's largest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, whose shares continued to recover after being sold heavily last week due to the resignation of three top executives in as many days.
"BHP continues to defy predictions of disaster after last week's events and I think we could see some of the institutions get back into the stock today," a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage said.
The dealer said there had been a reasonable amount of turnover in BHP early, indicating a possible return of institutional buying support which in turn could lift sentiment for the whole market.

"The market has been waiting for BHP to fall further but now that it hasn't happened I think some players are thinking to themselves I may be missing a chance to get back in on the rebound," the dealer said.
BHP shares were 16 cents higher at A$17.17 (US$12.71) after gaining two cents yesterday but falling about A$1 to A$16.99 in the last three sessions last week.
Stand-out issues in the first hour of trade included resources group WMC Ltd which was firmer ahead of the release of its annual results on Wednesday.
Dealers said the stock was bouncing from weakness after a recent re-weighting by the market which anticipates a fall in earnings from the company due mainly to lower base metal prices.
WMC shares were 10 cents higher at A$7.49 after falling 10 cents to A$7.39 on Monday.
Property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp Ltd continued to sag ahead of its full year earnings announcement on Thursday.
Lend Lease shares were 11.5 cents lower at A$29.30 after falling 63.5 cents to A$29.415 on Monday.
The company is expected to report a net profit rise of more than 10 percent for the year to June 30.
